articulation.label: ram
articulation.alt: ram: /r/ → /æ/ → /m/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /r/: Bunch the tongue; leave space at the ridge.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: nod
articulation.alt: nod: /n/ → /ɑ/ → /d/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /n/: Tip at the ridge; air goes through the nose.
/d/: Tip touches the ridge; add voice and release.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: tub
articulation.alt: tub: /t/ → /ʌ/ → /b/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
/b/: Close lips briefly; release into the next vowel.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: vet
articulation.alt: vet: /v/ → /ɛ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /v/: Upper teeth touch the lower lip; add voice.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: What can you do now?
sections: Match A, M, Z with a, m, z. Name the six printed forms in a mixed order.
Before any audio model, record your first reading of: rim · sob · tug · cob. Mark the vowel and blend from left to right.
Play the check audio. Choose sob or sub. Then play the separate dictation clip and write the word you hear.
Read “The cat is on the mat.” Explain where the cat is. Then make one clear request for a pen.
Compare your first attempt with the answers. Choose one sound or spelling pattern to review before A1.
Try again on another day without looking at the models. If you still need help, revisit the difficult letters, sounds or patterns. Clear, understandable speech matters more than copying an accent.

cards.answer: 1: A–a, M–m, Z–z. 2: rim /rɪm/, sob /sɑb/, tug /tʌɡ/, cob /kɑb/. These are new test words using taught short-vowel patterns. 3: sub /sʌb/. 4: The cat is on the mat; a possible request is “May I use your pen?” 5: Review the part you needed help with. Ask a listener or teacher to check whether your words are understandable. Dictation answer: tub /tʌb/.
